page.intro:
The Spotlight Assessment is a shorter, lower-cost way to understand why a child is finding reading, spelling or learning harder than expected, and what to do about it.

It takes around an hour and a half and can be carried out from age 6 — two years earlier than a full diagnostic assessment. It covers underlying ability, one area of cognitive processing (such as phonological processing or working memory), and word reading and spelling. You receive a short written report with specific recommendations for home and school.

### When is it the right choice?

- Your child is 6 or 7 and too young for a full diagnostic assessment
- You want a clear picture of strengths and difficulties, and practical next steps, without committing to a full assessment yet
- School has asked for more information to shape the support it provides

### What it does not do

A Spotlight Assessment does not provide a formal diagnosis of dyslexia, and cannot be used on its own for exam access arrangements or DSA. If a diagnosis is needed, a [full diagnostic assessment](/services/dyslexia-diagnostic-assessment/) is the right route, and the Spotlight results can inform it.
